class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Audit how this repository runs Muse Code and tighten its guardrails. Find every muse and muse exec invocation (scripts, CI, docs). Replace --yolo and --disable-sandbox with --disable-approval wherever the job isn&#x27;t a disposable container, never allow --yolo on pull-request or fork checkouts, add --sandbox-network restricted to jobs that don&#x27;t need the network, and write docs/muse-permissions.md listing each job&#x27;s posture and why.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Permissions and safety&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/permissions.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/permissions

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- Two independent layers: approval (risky tool calls wait for a decision) and an OS sandbox (writes only in the workspace and temp dir; .git, .muse and .agents stay read-only).
- --approval-mode on-request (default) passes recognized safe stages and holds dangerous ones (rm -rf forms, ripgrep -z, --pre, --hostname-bin); untrusted holds any shell stage without an allow rule; never holds nothing.
- Compound commands are reviewed stage by stage; rejecting a held stage runs nothing at all.
- --sandbox-network proxy-only (default: the first connection to a new host asks), restricted (none) or unrestricted.
- --yolo means no approval, no sandbox and a trusted workspace: it loads the checkout&#x27;s AGENTS.md, rules and skills, which on a PR or fork are attacker-controlled. --disable-sandbox also lets file tools write anywhere.

Starter code (Python)
import pathlib
import re

# List every Muse Code invocation that drops a guardrail, for the audit.
RISKY = re.compile(r&quot;--yolo|--disable-sandbox&quot;)
for path in pathlib.Path(&quot;.&quot;).rglob(&quot;*&quot;):
    if &quot;.git&quot; in path.parts or not path.is_file():
        continue
    try:
        text = path.read_text()
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, PermissionError):
        continue
    for n, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        if &quot;muse&quot; in line and RISKY.search(line):
            print(f&quot;{path}:{n}: {line.strip()}&quot;)

Done when
- `grep -rnE -- &quot;--yolo|--disable-sandbox&quot; .` matches only jobs documented as disposable containers, none triggered by pull requests.
- docs/muse-permissions.md lists every job with its flags and the reason for them.
- The key comes from META_API_KEY or a stored sign-in and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">2,970<!-- --> id="_R_95av5spfklb_" class="docs-toc-panel" hidden=""></div></nav></div><p class="docs-p">Grant Muse Code only the access you intend. Approval and sandboxing are on by default. The agent asks before any risky action, and every shell command runs inside an OS-enforced sandbox.</p><div class="docs-callout docs-callout-note" role="note"><span class="docs-callout-icon"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><circle cx="10" cy="10" r="8.5" fill="currentColor"></circle><path fill="#fff" d="M9.1 8.6h1.8v5.6H9.1z M10 5.3a1.1 1.1 0 1 1 0 2.2 1.1 1.1 0 0 1 0-2.2z"></path></svg></span><div class="docs-callout-body"><p class="docs-callout-title">Guardrails are on by default</p><p class="docs-p">Both guardrails are on unless you opt out. You can lower or remove them for a run in an isolated environment; see <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#run-without-guardrails">run without guardrails</a>.</p></div></div><h2 id="how-it-works" class="docs-h docs-h2">Two layers of control<a class="docs-anchor" href="#how-it-works" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Muse Code controls side effects at two independent layers:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Approval</strong>: before a tool call with side effects runs, the agent checks it against the approval policy. Safe actions pass automatically. Risky actions cause the harness to stop for your decision.</span></li><li><span><strong>Sandbox</strong>: shell commands run inside an OS-level sandbox. The sandbox limits filesystem writes and network access, and refuses to run if it cannot enforce that boundary.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">Each layer works on its own. If you disable one layer, the other stays in place.</p><p class="docs-p"><a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/workflows">Workflow</a> child agents inherit the lead session&#x27;s effective tools and permission boundary. A child can narrow that toolset through its agent definition, but it cannot expand it.</p><h2 id="profiles" class="docs-h docs-h2">Permission profiles<a class="docs-anchor" href="#profiles" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">A <strong>permission profile</strong> is the posture a session starts in. New sessions default to <strong>Auto-review</strong>:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Ask me</strong>: you decide every eligible approval request.</span></li><li><span><strong>Auto-review</strong>: the same access as Ask me, with an automated reviewer deciding eligible approval requests. When the reviewer is unavailable, it falls back to asking you. The reviewer is the <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#approval-modes">approval judge</a>.</span></li><li><span><strong>Unrestricted</strong>: no approval and no sandbox, with the workspace trusted for the run. This is the same posture as <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#run-without-guardrails"><code class="docs-code-inline">--yolo</code></a>, so use it only in an already-isolated environment.</span></li><li><span><strong>Read-only</strong>: the agent can read the workspace but not write files or run side-effecting commands.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">A profile sets the session&#x27;s overall posture; the <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#approval-modes">approval mode</a> and <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#approval-modes">approval judge</a> below are the finer controls it builds on. Ask me and Auto-review both run in the default <code class="docs-code-inline">on-request</code> mode, Ask me sends every eligible approval to you, while Auto-review lets the judge clear the ones it can.</p><p class="docs-p">Muse Code remembers your permission selections and applies them to new sessions. Set the profile a session starts in with the <code class="docs-code-inline">permissions.default_profile</code> setting in your <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/configuration#settings-file">settings file</a>.</p><p class="docs-p">If a profile has filesystem rules the session can&#x27;t enforce, such as extra file or home-directory paths, workspace subrules, or deny patterns, Muse Code refuses the profile when you select it and tells you why. To run such a profile read-only instead, set <code class="docs-code-inline">MUSE_PERMISSION_PROFILE_FAIL_OPEN=1</code>; Muse Code then shows a warning at startup.</p><h2 id="approval-modes" class="docs-h docs-h2">Choose an approval mode<a class="docs-anchor" href="#approval-modes" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Set the mode at launch with <code class="docs-code-inline">--approval-mode</code>:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">on-request</code></strong> (default): recognized, non-dangerous parsed shell stages normally pass without a prompt, and the <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#sandbox">sandbox</a> contains them. Dangerous or external-execution patterns stop for review. These include destructive removal forms and ripgrep options that can launch helper processes, such as <code class="docs-code-inline">-z</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">--search-zip</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">--pre</code>, and <code class="docs-code-inline">--hostname-bin</code>. Muse Code also checks wrappers around the command they launch.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">untrusted</code></strong>: this mode is stricter. A shell stage with no matching allow rule stops for review, not only the dangerous ones. It escalates shell execution only. File reads and in-workspace <code class="docs-code-inline">write_file</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">edit_file</code> writes still pass in any mode.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">never</code></strong>: nothing stops for approval. The sandbox alone contains what runs.</span></li></ul><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">bash</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="bash" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" style="background-color:transparent;color:var(--docs-syn-fg)" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">--approval-mode</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> untrusted</span></span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p">A built-in judge reviews prompt-bound calls automatically. Turn it off to send every review decision to you:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">bash</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="bash" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" style="background-color:transparent;color:var(--docs-syn-fg)" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">--approval-judge</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> off</span></span></code></pre></div></div><h2 id="staged-approvals" class="docs-h docs-h2">Review shell commands stage by stage<a class="docs-anchor" href="#staged-approvals" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Muse Code reviews a compound shell command one stage at a time, not as a single line. It parses the command into ordered stages, checks each one against policy, and blocks on the first stage it cannot approve.</p><p class="docs-p">Take this command:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">bash</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="bash" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" style="background-color:transparent;color:var(--docs-syn-fg)" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">wc </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">-l</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> report.log</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)"> &#x26;&#x26;</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> echo </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">cleaning</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)"> &#x26;&#x26;</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> rm </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">-rf</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> report.log</span></span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p"><code class="docs-code-inline">wc -l report.log</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">echo cleaning</code> are read-only, so they pass automatically. Muse Code classifies <code class="docs-code-inline">rm -rf report.log</code> as dangerous, so it holds for review at stage 3 of 3. The command runs as one unit only after every stage passes. If you reject the held stage, nothing runs, not even the safe stages before it.</p><p class="docs-p">How Muse Code treats a stage with no matching rule depends on the <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#approval-modes">approval mode</a>. A command that the parser cannot safely decompose, such as shell grouping or control flow that produces no reviewable stages, can also stop for review.</p><p class="docs-p">On Windows, agent-run commands go through PowerShell rather than Bash, and the same stage-by-stage review applies.</p><h2 id="trust-scopes" class="docs-h docs-h2">Grant trust at the right scope<a class="docs-anchor" href="#trust-scopes" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">When a stage holds, you choose how much trust to grant:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Allow once</strong>: run this stage one time only. Muse Code saves nothing.</span></li><li><span><strong>Always allow in this workspace</strong>: save a rule for this command&#x27;s prefix, scoped to this workspace root. The rule does not apply to other projects, and it does not cover a different command.</span></li><li><span><strong>Reject</strong>: deny the whole command.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">Prefix rules apply by specificity. A deny rule always overrides an allow rule, whatever the specificity. You cannot save an interpreter prefix such as <code class="docs-code-inline">python</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">bash</code>, or <code class="docs-code-inline">node</code> as a broad allow, because everything after the interpreter is arbitrary code.</p><p class="docs-p">The first time you open a workspace, Muse Code asks whether to trust it. When you trust a workspace, Muse Code loads its project-local skills, rules, and hooks. Muse Code remembers this trust for each workspace root.</p><p class="docs-p"><a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/session-messaging">Session messaging</a> has a separate peer-admission boundary. Exact-profile peers can be admitted automatically; unverified or non-matching senders may trigger a prompt. A message from another session cannot approve tools, grant consent, or change this session&#x27;s permissions.</p><h2 id="sandbox" class="docs-h docs-h2">Run inside the sandbox<a class="docs-anchor" href="#sandbox" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Shell commands run inside a filesystem and network policy that the operating system enforces. On macOS the policy uses Seatbelt. On Linux it uses a bundled bubblewrap helper. On Windows it uses a Windows sandbox that can request administrator approval (a UAC prompt) the first time it initializes; normal use does not require running as administrator. The policy grants write access to the workspace and a temp directory, and keeps the rest of the filesystem read-only. Inside the writable workspace, the <code class="docs-code-inline">.git</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">.muse</code>, and <code class="docs-code-inline">.agents</code> directories stay read-only, so the agent can&#x27;t rewrite its own history, configuration, or memory.</p><p class="docs-p">Muse Code refuses to run a shell command when it can&#x27;t confirm that the sandbox is active. On Linux, Muse Code checks the sandbox helper first. A host without a working bubblewrap fails every shell command as an environment error, as does a musl build that ships without the helper. On macOS, Muse Code verifies Seatbelt once, at session startup.</p><p class="docs-p">A write outside the allowed roots fails at the OS level:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">text</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="text" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line">$ echo data &gt; $HOME/notes.txt</span>
<span class="line">/bin/bash: line 1: /home/you/notes.txt: Read-only file system</span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p">Control network access with <code class="docs-code-inline">--sandbox-network</code>:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">proxy-only</code></strong> (default): Muse Code approves outbound connections per destination. The first connection to a new host, port, or protocol stops for review, like a shell command.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">restricted</code></strong>: no network access.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">unrestricted</code></strong>: full network access. The earlier name, <code class="docs-code-inline">enabled</code>, still works but is deprecated.</span></li></ul><h2 id="run-without-guardrails" class="docs-h docs-h2">Run without guardrails<a class="docs-anchor" href="#run-without-guardrails" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">For a run inside an already-isolated environment, you can lower or remove the guardrails:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--yolo</code></strong>: disable approval and the sandbox, and trust the workspace, for this run. This is the same posture as the <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#profiles">Unrestricted profile</a>.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--disable-approval</code></strong>: keep the sandbox, but skip approval prompts.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--disable-sandbox</code></strong>: keep approval, but skip the sandbox. This flag also removes workspace confinement from the file tools, so <code class="docs-code-inline">write_file</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">edit_file</code> can write anywhere on the filesystem. It also forces the network to full egress and overrides <code class="docs-code-inline">--sandbox-network</code>.</span></li></ul><div class="docs-callout docs-callout-warning" role="note"><span class="docs-callout-icon"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path fill="currentColor" d="M8.6 2.8a1.6 1.6 0 0 1 2.8 0l6.9 12a1.6 1.6 0 0 1-1.4 2.4H3.1a1.6 1.6 0 0 1-1.4-2.4l6.9-12z"></path><path fill="#fff" d="M9.1 6.8h1.8l-.2 5.2H9.3z M10 13.2a1 1 0 1 1 0 2 1 1 0 0 1 0-2z"></path></svg></span><div class="docs-callout-body"><p class="docs-callout-title">Use --yolo only when isolated</p><p class="docs-p">Use <code class="docs-code-inline">--yolo</code> only where you already trust both the environment and the code, such as a disposable CI container. Never use it on a workstation with access to real credentials or infrastructure. <code class="docs-code-inline">--yolo</code> removes both layers and trusts the workspace, so it loads the checkout&#x27;s <code class="docs-code-inline">AGENTS.md</code>, rules, and skills. On a pull-request or fork checkout, those files are attacker-controlled instructions.</p></div></div><h2 id="next-steps" class="docs-h docs-h2">Next steps<a class="docs-anchor" href="#next-steps" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Distribute work across a team of agents under the same guardrails with <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#multi-agent">multi-agent orchestration</a>.</span></li><li><span>Run structured agent groups within this boundary with <a class="docs-link" class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Audit how this repository runs Muse Code and tighten its guardrails. Find every muse and muse exec invocation (scripts, CI, docs). Replace --yolo and --disable-sandbox with --disable-approval wherever the job isn&#x27;t a disposable container, never allow --yolo on pull-request or fork checkouts, add --sandbox-network restricted to jobs that don&#x27;t need the network, and write docs/muse-permissions.md listing each job&#x27;s posture and why.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Permissions and safety&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/permissions.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/permissions

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- Two independent layers: approval (risky tool calls wait for a decision) and an OS sandbox (writes only in the workspace and temp dir; .git, .muse and .agents stay read-only).
- --approval-mode on-request (default) passes recognized safe stages and holds dangerous ones (rm -rf forms, ripgrep -z, --pre, --hostname-bin); untrusted holds any shell stage without an allow rule; never holds nothing.
- Compound commands are reviewed stage by stage; rejecting a held stage runs nothing at all.
- --sandbox-network proxy-only (default: the first connection to a new host asks), restricted (none) or unrestricted.
- --yolo means no approval, no sandbox and a trusted workspace: it loads the checkout&#x27;s AGENTS.md, rules and skills, which on a PR or fork are attacker-controlled. --disable-sandbox also lets file tools write anywhere.

Starter code (Python)
import pathlib
import re

# List every Muse Code invocation that drops a guardrail, for the audit.
RISKY = re.compile(r&quot;--yolo|--disable-sandbox&quot;)
for path in pathlib.Path(&quot;.&quot;).rglob(&quot;*&quot;):
    if &quot;.git&quot; in path.parts or not path.is_file():
        continue
    try:
        text = path.read_text()
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, PermissionError):
        continue
    for n, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        if &quot;muse&quot; in line and RISKY.search(line):
            print(f&quot;{path}:{n}: {line.strip()}&quot;)

Done when
- `grep -rnE -- &quot;--yolo|--disable-sandbox&quot; .` matches only jobs documented as disposable containers, none triggered by pull requests.
- docs/muse-permissions.md lists every job with its flags and the reason for them.
- The key comes from META_API_KEY or a stored sign-in and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">2,970<!-- --> characters</span><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-primary docs-btn-sm"><svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy prompt</span></button></div></div></div><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" title="Copy this page as Markdown"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy page</span></button><a class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" href="https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/permissions" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M14 4h6v6 M20 4l-9 9 M18 14v4.5a1.5 1.5 0 0 1-1.5 1.5h-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 4 18.5v-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 5.5 6H10"></path></svg><span>View on dev.meta.ai</span><span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a><p class="docs-rail-note">Independent concept built on Meta&#x27;s Model API.
